Segment C

After segment B there is a gap of unknown length. Col. ii of the OB manuscript I is tentatively placed here as segment C, because Seg. C 1 seems to be parallel to Seg. A 16 and Seg. S+T+-NA vi ----

Manuscript I iv 13–19 contains a reaction of Enki/Ea to a speech of Atra-ḫasīs. Since these lines follow directly manuscript I iv 12 = Seg. E 161, the end of a long speech of Atra-ḫasīs to Enki/Ea, it is most natural to assume that this reaction has to be placed here as Seg. E 161k–161r. The three manuscripts D, H and S+T+-NA skip these lines and jump directly to another speech of Atra-ḫasīs reported by the messengers to Enki/Ea (Seg. E 162ff.).

Segment F

After Seg. E there is a lacuna of unknown length. We estimate that manuscript D had 55–58 lines in each column. This means that between Seg. E 168 and Seg. G 1, 23–26 lines are missing in D. If manuscript I v is rightly placed here as Seg. F, as we believe, only 5–6 lines are missing before and after Seg. F. Note however that it is not certain that manuscript I and D had exactly the same text.

Translation

Seg. A 1 1200 (Q-NA: [36]00) years had not yet passed,

Seg. A 2 when the population of the country had grown numerous and the people multiplied.

Seg. A 3 The land was bellowing like a bull.

Seg. A 4 The god was disturbed with their uproar (bd: clamor; Q-NA: the [g]ods descended).

Seg. A 5 Enlil heard their clamor (Q-NA, S+T+-NA: summoned his assembly).

Seg. A 6 He addressed the great gods (Q-NA, S+T+-NA: the gods, his sons):

Seg. A 6a “Did you put on them a bad fate?

Seg. A 6b The people did not diminish, but have become more numerous than before!

Seg. A 7 The noise of mankind has become too intense for me (S+T+-NA: I got disturbed by their clamor),

Seg. A 8 With their uproar, I am deprived of sleep (S+T+-NA: sleep does not overcome).

Seg. A 9 Cut off sustenance for the people.

Seg. A 10 Let plants be to satisfy their hunger (bd, S+T+-NA: for their belly) in short supply.

Seg. A 11 (S+T+-NA: Above,) Adad should withhold (S+T+-NA: make scarce) his rain.

Seg. A 12 Let the flood not come up pleasantly (S+T-NA: Below, let the flood be blocked and not rise)

Seg. A 13 from the abyss.

Seg. A 14 Let the wind blow

Seg. A 15 and parch the ground.

Seg. A 16 Let the clouds grow thicker and thicker

Seg. A 17 but not release a drop.

Seg. A 18 Let the fields withhold their yields.

Seg. A 19 Let Nisaba stop up (S+T+-NA: turn away) her breast.

Seg. A 20 Let there be no rejoicing for them.

Seg. A 21 Let [...] be gloomy.

Seg. A 22 May there not [...].

Seg. A 23 [...]

Seg. B 1 Let the black fields become white.

Seg. B 2 Let the broad plain produce salt.

Seg. B 3 Let the earth turn upside down its womb.

Seg. B 4 Let no vegetables shoot up, no pulse grow.

Seg. B 5 Let pestilence be laid on the people.

Seg. B 6 Let the womb be constricted and give no easy birth to a child.”

Seg. B 7 They cut off food supplies from the people.

Seg. B 8 Vegetables were sparse in their stomachs.

Seg. B 9 Adad above made his rain scarce.

Seg. B 10 Below, high water was blocked (and) did not rise from the depths.

Seg. B 11 The fields withheld their yields.

Seg. B 12 Nisaba turned away her breast.

Seg. B 13 The black fields became white.

Seg. B 14 The broad plain produced salt.

Seg. B 15 Earth turned upside down its womb.

Seg. B 16 No vegetables shot up, no pulse grew.

Seg. B 17 Pestilence was laid upon the people.

Seg. B 18 The womb was constricted and did not give easy birth to a child.

Seg. C 1 grew thicker and thicker(?).

Seg. C 2 [... a]byss(?).

Seg. C ii 3 [..]. let us throw(?).

Seg. C ii 4 […] …

Seg. C ii 5 […] …

Seg. C ii 6 […] …

Seg. C ii 7 […] …

Seg. D 1 Blood congealed(?).

Seg. D 2 The belly was bloated.

Seg. D 3 He could not think.

Seg. D 4 The animal(s) had stomach-cramp.

Seg. D 5 It was unable to open its mouth.

Seg. D 6 Humankind had stomach-cramp, with weeping voice.

Seg. D 7 Then the sage Atra-ḫasīs

Seg. D 8 saw (all that and) spoke to Ea, his lord:
